key_insight: 4D flow MRI captures overall carotid flow patterns, but it systematically underestimates plaque-surface wall shear stress compared with patient-specific CFD, especially in more severe stenosis and at key bifurcation locations.
engineering_relevance: For hemodynamic risk assessment and carotid plaque studies, MRI-only WSS estimates may be insufficient without CFD-style correction or validation, particularly when local stress magnitude matters.
method: 240 carotid arteries from 120 patients were analyzed using patient-specific CFD geometries and boundary conditions derived from MRI.
Peak-systolic velocity and circumferential WSS were compared at three standardized cross-sections; plaque-surface WSS was evaluated in 63 stenosed arteries with reliable plaque segmentation.
Agreement was quantified with Bland-Altman analysis, Spearman correlation, and exploratory multivariable regression of WSS discrepancies.
evidence_signal: MRI underestimated plaque-surface mean and maximum WSS by 40.9 ± 28.8% and 44.5 ± 26.8%, with discrepancies increasing with stenosis degree (ρ = 0.47 and 0.50).
watch_item: The plaque-surface WSS comparison was limited to 63 arteries with reliable plaque segmentation, and the regression findings were exploratory rather than definitive.
paper_title: Comparative Evaluation of Carotid Artery Hemodynamics: Patient-Specific CFD Simulations vs. 4D flow MRI
